_comment: Source of truth for statements. A statement with "status": "candidate" is answered by audits but not asked in the test until audits show it is contested (audits/statements/STANDARD.md). Adding or removing a statement leaves existing audits valid; rewording one needs a new id. The agree/disagree/note/icon fields explain each statement to test takers and do not affect audits.

statements.text: The government should provide universal healthcare.
statements.agree: Everyone gets health care paid for or guaranteed by the state, usually through taxes.
statements.disagree: The government should not provide universal healthcare.
statements.note: About how far the state should guarantee basic services.

statements.text: The minimum wage should be raised substantially.
statements.agree: The legal lowest wage goes up a lot, even if some employers have to pay more.
statements.disagree: The minimum wage should not be raised substantially.
statements.note: About how much the state should set pay.

statements.text: Free markets allocate resources better than governments do.
statements.agree: Prices and competition generally decide better than officials what gets made and who gets it.
statements.disagree: Free markets do not allocate resources better than governments do.
statements.note: A core economic question: markets or the state.

statements.text: Major industries like energy, rail and utilities should be publicly owned.
statements.agree: Key industries are run by the state or public bodies instead of private companies.
statements.disagree: Major industries like energy, rail and utilities should not be publicly owned.
statements.note: About who owns the commanding heights of the economy.

statements.text: Taxes on the wealthy should be significantly higher.
statements.agree: High earners and the very rich pay a noticeably larger share in tax.
statements.disagree: Taxes on the wealthy should not be significantly higher.
statements.note: About redistribution through taxes.

statements.text: Labor unions are good for workers and for society.
statements.agree: Workers organizing collectively improves pay, conditions and fairness overall.
statements.disagree: Labor unions are not good for workers and for society.
statements.note: About organized labor's role.

statements.text: Private property is a fundamental right that should be very hard to override.
statements.agree: Owners' rights to their property should almost never be overridden, even for public goals.
statements.disagree: Private property is not a fundamental right that should be very hard to override.
statements.note: About how absolute property rights are.

statements.text: Corporations should be more tightly regulated.
statements.agree: Companies face more rules on things like pollution, prices, labor and competition.
statements.disagree: Corporations should not be more tightly regulated.
statements.note: About the state's oversight of business.

statements.text: Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.
statements.agree: Benefits often discourage work and should be reduced.
statements.disagree: Welfare programs should not be cut on the grounds that they create dependency.
statements.note: About the size of the welfare state.

statements.text: Workers should collectively own the businesses they work in.
statements.agree: Businesses should belong to the people who work in them, for example as cooperatives.
statements.disagree: Workers should not collectively own the businesses they work in.
statements.note: About who owns workplaces.

statements.text: Government surveillance is acceptable if it prevents terrorism.
statements.agree: Security agencies may monitor communications if it helps stop attacks.
statements.disagree: Government surveillance is not acceptable even if it prevents terrorism.
statements.note: About security versus civil liberties.

statements.text: Recreational drugs should be legal for adults.
statements.agree: Adults may legally buy and use drugs such as cannabis, possibly with regulation.
statements.disagree: Recreational drugs should be illegal for adults.
statements.note: About personal freedom versus protection from harm.

statements.text: Hate speech should be legally restricted.
statements.agree: Speech that attacks groups for who they are can be punished by law.
statements.disagree: Hate speech should be legal.
statements.note: About limits on free speech.

statements.text: A strong leader who can bypass political gridlock would benefit the country.
statements.agree: A decisive leader who can get past political deadlock would help.
statements.disagree: A strong leader who can bypass political gridlock would not benefit the country.
statements.note: About concentrated versus limited power.

statements.text: The state itself is unnecessary and harmful.
statements.agree: Society would be better off without governments at all.
statements.disagree: The state itself is not unnecessary and harmful.
statements.note: Separates anarchists from everyone else.

statements.text: Gun ownership should be strictly limited.
statements.agree: Gun ownership should be strictly limited by law.
statements.disagree: Gun ownership should not be strictly limited.
statements.note: About gun rights versus gun control.

statements.text: The police and military need more funding and authority.
statements.agree: Police and armed forces get bigger budgets and more powers.
statements.disagree: The police and military do not need more funding and authority.
statements.note: About security institutions.

statements.text: Sex work between consenting adults should be legal.
statements.agree: Adults can legally sell sexual services, ideally with rules for safety.
statements.disagree: Sex work between consenting adults should be illegal.
statements.note: About personal freedom, morality and exploitation.

statements.text: Decisions should be made as locally as possible rather than by national government.
statements.agree: Towns and regions make most decisions rather than the national government.
statements.disagree: Local decision-making should not take priority over decisions by the national government.
statements.note: About decentralization.

statements.text: Prisons should focus on rehabilitation rather than punishment.
statements.agree: Prisons mainly try to help offenders change and return to society.
statements.disagree: Prisons should not put rehabilitation ahead of punishment.
statements.note: About the purpose of criminal justice.

statements.text: Traditional family structures are the foundation of a healthy society.
statements.agree: Traditional family structures are what a healthy society rests on.
statements.disagree: Traditional family structures are not the foundation of a healthy society.
statements.note: About social traditionalism.

statements.text: Same-sex marriage should be legal.
statements.agree: Same-sex couples can marry with the same rights as anyone else.
statements.disagree: The law should not extend marriage to same-sex couples.
statements.note: About LGBT equality and tradition.

statements.text: Abortion should be legal in most cases.
statements.agree: Women can legally choose to end most pregnancies.
statements.disagree: Abortion should be illegal in most cases.
statements.note: About reproductive rights and the status of the unborn.

statements.text: Religion should play a larger role in public life.
statements.agree: Religious values and institutions should shape laws, schools and public life more.
statements.disagree: Religion should not play a larger role in public life.
statements.note: About religion in public life.

statements.text: Society should actively work to correct historical racial injustices.
statements.agree: Society should take active steps, such as targeted programs, to repair past discrimination.
statements.disagree: Society should not actively work to correct historical racial injustices.
statements.note: About how to deal with historical racism.

statements.text: Gender is primarily a social construct.
statements.agree: Ideas of what men and women are like come mostly from culture, not biology.
statements.disagree: Gender is not primarily a social construct.
statements.note: About gender and tradition.

statements.text: Preserving national culture and traditions is important.
statements.agree: Protecting the nation's language, customs and heritage matters.
statements.disagree: Preserving national culture and traditions is not important.
statements.note: About national identity.

statements.text: Social change should be gradual and respect established institutions.
statements.agree: Reform should be slow and build on existing institutions.
statements.disagree: Social change should not be gradual and respect established institutions.
statements.note: About the pace of change: conservative or radical.

statements.text: Immigration levels should be reduced.
statements.agree: Fewer people should be allowed to move into the country.
statements.disagree: Immigration levels should not be reduced.
statements.note: About immigration.

statements.text: International organizations like the UN should have more power.
statements.agree: Bodies like the UN should be able to make more binding decisions over countries.
statements.disagree: International organizations like the UN should not have more power.
statements.note: About global governance versus sovereignty.

statements.text: Free trade benefits everyone in the long run.
statements.agree: Fewer tariffs and trade barriers make all countries better off over time.
statements.disagree: Free trade does not benefit everyone in the long run.
statements.note: About globalization.

statements.text: My country should put its own interests ahead of global cooperation.
statements.agree: Your country's own interests come before international agreements.
statements.disagree: My country should not put its own interests ahead of global cooperation.
statements.note: About nationalism versus internationalism.

statements.text: Military intervention abroad is sometimes necessary to protect human rights.
statements.agree: Using force abroad can be right to stop mass atrocities.
statements.disagree: Military intervention abroad is not necessary to protect human rights.
statements.note: About foreign policy.

statements.text: National borders should eventually be open.
statements.agree: In the long run people should be free to live and work in any country.
statements.disagree: National borders should not eventually be open.
statements.note: About borders as such.

statements.text: Economic growth should be limited to protect the environment.
statements.agree: Protecting nature can mean accepting less economic growth.
statements.disagree: Economic growth should not be limited for the sake of the environment.
statements.note: About growth versus ecology.

statements.text: Climate change requires drastic government action.
statements.agree: Governments should act fast and hard on emissions, even at real cost.
statements.disagree: Climate change does not require drastic government action.
statements.note: About climate change.

statements.text: Technological progress will solve most of humanity's problems.
statements.agree: Science and technology will fix most of what goes wrong for people.
statements.disagree: Technology will not solve most of humanity's problems.
statements.note: About optimism about technology.

statements.text: Nuclear power should be expanded.
statements.agree: Build more nuclear power plants.
statements.disagree: Nuclear power should not be expanded.
statements.note: About energy policy; splits even environmentalists.

statements.text: Revolution is sometimes justified to achieve political change.
statements.agree: Revolution can sometimes be justified to achieve political change.
statements.disagree: Revolution is not justified to achieve political change.
statements.note: About revolution versus reform.

statements.text: Experts should have more say in policy than the general public.
statements.agree: Specialists should have more weight in decisions than public opinion.
statements.disagree: Experts should not have more say in policy than the general public.
statements.note: About technocracy versus democracy.

statements.text: A centrally planned economy can work better than a market economy.
statements.agree: A planned economy, where the state decides production, can outperform markets.
statements.disagree: A centrally planned economy cannot work better than a market economy.
statements.note: Separates planned-economy socialism from other views.

statements.text: Markets are acceptable as long as businesses are owned by their workers or the public.
statements.agree: Firms can compete in markets as long as workers or the public own them.
statements.disagree: Markets are not made acceptable just by worker or public ownership of businesses.
statements.note: Identifies market socialism.

statements.text: A tax on the value of land should replace most other taxes.
statements.agree: Taxing the value of land, not work or trade, should fund most of government.
statements.disagree: A tax on land value should not replace most other taxes.
statements.note: Identifies Georgism.

statements.text: Large inheritances should be heavily taxed.
statements.agree: Large inheritances should be taxed heavily.
statements.disagree: Large inheritances should not be heavily taxed.
statements.note: About inherited wealth.

statements.text: Every adult should receive an unconditional basic income from the state.
statements.agree: Every adult gets a regular payment from the state, whether or not they work.
statements.disagree: Every adult should not receive an unconditional basic income from the state.
statements.note: About universal basic income.

statements.text: Tariffs should protect domestic industry from foreign competition.
statements.agree: Taxes on imports should shield domestic producers from foreign competition.
statements.disagree: Tariffs should not be used to protect domestic industry from foreign competition.
statements.note: About protectionism.

statements.text: The state should direct investment toward strategic industries.
statements.agree: The government should steer money into industries it considers important.
statements.disagree: The state should not direct investment toward strategic industries.
statements.note: About industrial policy.

statements.text: Property should be spread widely among small owners rather than concentrated in corporations or the state.
statements.agree: Most people should own some land, a shop or a small business.
statements.disagree: Widespread small ownership should not take priority over concentration of property in corporations or the state.
statements.note: Identifies distributism.

statements.text: Money and wage labor should eventually be abolished.
statements.agree: Eventually people should work and share without money or wages.
statements.disagree: Money and wage labor should not eventually be abolished.
statements.note: Identifies communism and anarcho-communism.

statements.text: Central banks should be abolished and money left to the market.
statements.agree: End central banks and let private money or free banking take over.
statements.disagree: Central banks should not be abolished.
statements.note: About monetary policy; identifies some libertarians.

statements.text: Employers and workers should be organized into state-recognized bodies that set wages and prices together.
statements.agree: Officially recognized bodies of employers and workers should set wages and prices together.
statements.disagree: Wages and prices should not be set by state-recognised bodies of employers and workers.
statements.note: Identifies corporatism.

statements.text: A single party guided by the correct ideology should lead the state.
statements.agree: One party with the right ideology should govern without rival parties.
statements.disagree: A single party guided by the correct ideology should not lead the state.
statements.note: About one-party states.

statements.text: A hereditary monarch can be a legitimate and good head of state.
statements.agree: A hereditary monarch, whether a ceremonial figure or the actual ruler, can be a good head of state.
statements.disagree: A hereditary monarch cannot be a legitimate and good head of state.
statements.note: About monarchy.

statements.text: Democracy is the best form of government, even when voters choose badly.
statements.agree: Democracy is best even when voters make poor choices.
statements.disagree: Democracy is not the best form of government when voters choose badly.
statements.note: About commitment to democracy.

statements.text: Citizens should vote directly on major laws rather than leaving them to representatives.
statements.agree: Citizens should decide major laws themselves through referendums.
statements.disagree: Citizens should not vote directly on major laws.
statements.note: About direct versus representative democracy.

statements.text: Workers' councils, not parliaments, should be the basis of political power.
statements.agree: Power should come from councils elected in workplaces, not from parliaments.
statements.disagree: Workers' councils should not replace parliaments as the basis of political power.
statements.note: Identifies council communism and some socialists.

statements.text: Regions should have the right to secede from the country.
statements.agree: Regions should be able to leave the country.
statements.disagree: Regions should have no right to secede from the country.
statements.note: About self-determination.

statements.text: Some people are naturally better suited to rule than others.
statements.agree: Some people are better suited by nature to govern.
statements.disagree: Some people are not naturally better suited to rule than others.
statements.note: About hierarchy and equality.

statements.text: Political violence is never justified.
statements.agree: Violence is never an acceptable way to pursue political goals.
statements.disagree: Political violence is sometimes justified.
statements.note: About political violence.

statements.text: War can strengthen a nation's character.
statements.agree: Fighting wars can make a nation stronger and more united.
statements.disagree: War does not strengthen a nation's character.
statements.note: About militarism.

statements.text: Religion and the state should be strictly separated.
statements.agree: Religion and government should have nothing to do with each other.
statements.disagree: Religion and the state should not be strictly separated.
statements.note: About secularism.

statements.text: Laws should be based on religious scripture.
statements.agree: Laws should follow religious texts.
statements.disagree: Laws should not be based on religious scripture.
statements.note: Identifies theocracy.

statements.text: Courts, policing and defense could be provided by private companies.
statements.agree: Security and justice could be bought from competing private providers.
statements.disagree: Courts, policing and defense could not be provided by private companies.
statements.note: Identifies anarcho-capitalism.

statements.text: My country should maintain military superiority over its rivals.
statements.agree: Your country should be militarily stronger than its rivals.
statements.disagree: My country should not maintain military superiority over its rivals.
statements.note: About hawkish foreign policy.

statements.text: A nation should be made up mainly of one ethnic group.
statements.agree: A nation should be mainly one ethnic people.
statements.disagree: A nation should not be made up mainly of one ethnic group.
statements.note: Identifies ethnic nationalism.

statements.text: Class conflict is the main driving force of history.
statements.agree: History is mainly driven by conflict between economic classes.
statements.disagree: Class conflict is not the main driving force of history.
statements.note: Identifies Marxist thinking.

statements.text: Society should aim for equality of outcomes, not only of opportunity.
statements.agree: Society should aim for people to end up with similar levels of wealth and well-being.
statements.disagree: Society should not aim for equality of outcomes as well as of opportunity.
statements.note: About kinds of equality.

statements.text: Indigenous peoples should have authority over their traditional lands.
statements.agree: Indigenous peoples should control their traditional territories.
statements.disagree: Indigenous peoples should not have authority over their traditional lands.
statements.note: About indigenous rights.

statements.text: Former colonial powers owe reparations to the nations they colonized.
statements.agree: Countries that had colonies should compensate the countries they colonized.
statements.disagree: Former colonial powers do not owe reparations to the nations they colonized.
statements.note: About historical justice between nations.

statements.text: Nations that share a religion or civilization should unite politically.
statements.agree: Countries with a shared religion or civilization should join politically.
statements.disagree: Nations that share a religion or civilization should not unite politically.
statements.note: Identifies pan-Islamism, Eurasianism and similar movements.

statements.text: Pursuing your own self-interest is morally good.
statements.agree: Looking after your own interests is right, not just allowed.
statements.disagree: Pursuing your own self-interest is not morally good.
statements.note: Identifies Objectivism and egoism.

statements.text: Citizens' duties to their community come before their individual rights.
statements.agree: What you owe your community matters more than your personal rights.
statements.disagree: Citizens' duties to their community do not come before their individual rights.
statements.note: About communitarianism versus individualism.

statements.text: Nature has value in itself, apart from its usefulness to humans.
statements.agree: Nature matters for its own sake, not only because it is useful to people.
statements.disagree: Nature does not have value in itself, apart from its usefulness to humans.
statements.note: Identifies deep ecology.

statements.text: Population growth should be actively limited.
statements.agree: Governments should actively slow population growth.
statements.disagree: Population growth should not be actively limited.
statements.note: Identifies Malthusian views.

statements.text: Industrial civilization has been a disaster for humanity.
statements.agree: Industrial society has done more harm than good to humanity.
statements.disagree: Industrial civilization has not been a disaster for humanity.
statements.note: Identifies anarcho-primitivism.

statements.text: Society should speed up technological change even if it disrupts existing institutions.
statements.agree: Speed up technological change even if it upends existing institutions.
statements.disagree: Society should not speed up technological change if it disrupts existing institutions.
statements.note: Identifies accelerationism.

statements.text: People should be free to enhance their bodies and minds with technology.
statements.agree: People may use technology to improve their bodies and minds.
statements.disagree: People should not be free to enhance their bodies and minds with technology.
statements.note: About transhumanism versus bioconservatism.

statements.text: AI and algorithms should take over more government decision-making.
statements.agree: Let AI and algorithms make more public decisions.
statements.disagree: AI and algorithms should not take over more government decision-making.
statements.note: About technocracy and automation.

statements.text: People should be able to use encryption the government cannot break.
statements.agree: People should be able to keep their communications private, even from government.
statements.disagree: People should not be able to use encryption the government cannot break.
statements.note: About digital privacy; identifies crypto-anarchism.

statements.text: Restoring a lost social order matters more than pursuing progress.
statements.agree: Recovering how society used to be matters more than moving forward.
statements.disagree: Restoring a lost social order does not matter more than pursuing progress.
statements.note: Identifies reactionary thought.

statements.text: Policies should be judged by their results, not by whether they fit an ideology.
statements.agree: Use whatever works, regardless of which ideology it comes from.
statements.disagree: Results should not take priority over ideological fit in judging policies.
statements.note: About pragmatism versus principle.

statements.text: Political change should come through direct action rather than through elections and parliaments.
statements.agree: Strikes, occupations and organizing outside the system change things; voting mostly doesn't.
statements.disagree: Direct action should not replace elections and parliaments as the way to political change.
statements.note: About working inside or outside electoral politics.

statements.text: The methods used to change society should reflect the society one wants to create.
statements.agree: You can't reach a free, fair society by unfree or unfair means.
statements.disagree: The methods used to change society should not reflect the society one wants to create.
statements.note: About whether ends justify means.

statements.text: Humanity would be better off returning to a hunter-gatherer way of life.
statements.agree: Agriculture and civilization made life worse; foraging societies lived better.
statements.disagree: Humanity would not be better off returning to a hunter-gatherer way of life.
statements.note: About rejecting civilization itself.

statements.text: The division of labor should be abolished.
statements.agree: People shouldn't be locked into one specialized job for life.
statements.disagree: The division of labor should not be abolished.
statements.note: About specialized work.

statements.text: Goods should ultimately be distributed according to each person's needs rather than their work or wealth.
statements.agree: Everyone should get what they need, whatever they contribute.
statements.disagree: Goods should not ultimately be distributed by need ahead of work or wealth.
statements.note: About distribution in a future society.

statements.text: Goods and services should be produced to meet people's needs rather than to make a profit.
statements.agree: The economy should be organized around what people need, not what sells at a profit.
statements.disagree: Meeting people's needs should not take priority over making a profit in producing goods and services.
statements.note: About the purpose of production.

statements.text: Profit made from owning businesses comes from exploiting the workers who produce it.
statements.agree: Owners' profit is value taken from workers' labor.
statements.disagree: Profit made from owning businesses does not come from exploiting the workers who produce it.
statements.note: About where profit comes from.

statements.text: After a revolution, the working class should hold dictatorial power over the former ruling classes until classes disappear.
statements.agree: A workers' state must suppress the old ruling class for a time.
statements.disagree: After a revolution, the working class should not hold dictatorial power over the former ruling classes until classes disappear.
statements.note: About the transition after a revolution.

statements.text: Agricultural land should be farmed collectively rather than by individual farmers.
statements.agree: Farms should be collective or cooperative enterprises.
statements.disagree: Collective farming should not replace farming by individual farmers.
statements.note: About who works the land.

statements.text: Capitalism inevitably leads to imperialism and wars between the great powers.
statements.agree: Competition for markets and resources drives capitalist states to war.
statements.disagree: Capitalism does not inevitably lead to imperialism and wars between the great powers.
statements.note: About the causes of war.

statements.text: Taxation is a form of theft or forced labor.
statements.agree: Taking people's earnings by force is wrong, whatever it pays for.
statements.disagree: Taxation is not theft or forced labor.
statements.note: About whether taxation is legitimate at all.

statements.text: The state may restrict what adults do only to prevent harm to others.
statements.agree: Choices that harm no one else should never be crimes.
statements.disagree: The state may restrict what adults do for reasons other than preventing harm to others.
statements.note: About the limits of state power over individuals.

statements.text: Rights belong to individuals, not to groups.
statements.agree: Only individuals have rights; groups have none of their own.
statements.disagree: Rights can belong to groups as well as to individuals.
statements.note: About who rights belong to.

statements.text: The government should be able to conscript citizens into military service.
statements.agree: Defending the country can be required of citizens.
statements.disagree: Military service should always be voluntary.
statements.note: About compulsory military service.

statements.text: The freedom to leave a country is a more important check on government than the right to vote.
statements.agree: People keep governments honest best by being able to leave.
statements.disagree: The freedom to leave a country is not a more important check on government than the right to vote.
statements.note: About exit versus voice.

statements.text: Governments should be run like businesses, with citizens treated as customers who can leave.
statements.agree: The state should be run like a company, with citizens as customers who can leave.
statements.disagree: Governments should not be run like businesses, with citizens treated as customers who can leave.
statements.note: Identifies neocameralism.

statements.text: Freedom requires that people have the material means to act on it, not only the absence of interference.
statements.agree: Being free includes having the resources, education and security to act on your choices.
statements.disagree: Freedom does not require that people have the material means to act on it, beyond the absence of interference.
statements.note: About what freedom means.

statements.text: Universities and the news media together hold more real political power than elected officials.
statements.agree: The real power lies with academia and the press, not the people elected.
statements.disagree: Universities and the news media do not together hold more real political power than elected officials.
statements.note: About where power really lies.

statements.text: Average differences in ability between racial groups are largely genetic.
statements.agree: Group differences in ability are mostly inherited.
statements.disagree: Average differences in ability between racial groups are not largely genetic.
statements.note: About the causes of group differences, a position some ideologies are defined by.

statements.text: Citizens should be represented through families, local communities and trade bodies rather than through political parties.
statements.agree: Society's natural groups, not parties, should be the basis of representation.
statements.disagree: Representation through families, local communities and trade bodies should not replace representation through political parties.
statements.note: Identifies corporatist and 'organic' democracy.

statements.text: The state should direct every area of life, including culture, education and the economy.
statements.agree: Nothing should lie outside the state's direction.
statements.disagree: The state should not direct every area of life, including culture, education and the economy.
statements.note: Identifies totalitarianism.

statements.text: The nation needs a radical rebirth to overcome a period of decadence.
statements.agree: The nation has decayed and must be reborn.
statements.disagree: The nation does not need a radical rebirth to overcome decadence.
statements.note: About national decline and renewal.

statements.text: A strong nation should expand its territory and influence abroad.
statements.agree: Great nations grow, including by gaining territory.
statements.disagree: A strong nation should not expand its territory and influence abroad.
statements.note: About expansionism.

statements.text: Political authority should rest on personal oaths of loyalty between lords and their followers.
statements.agree: Authority should rest on personal oaths of loyalty between lords and their followers.
statements.disagree: Political authority should not rest on personal oaths of loyalty between lords and their followers.
statements.note: Identifies feudalism.

statements.text: Those who farm the land should be legally bound to it and owe labor to its lord.
statements.agree: Peasants owe labor to the lord whose land they live on.
statements.disagree: Those who farm the land should not be legally bound to it and owe labor to its lord.
statements.note: Identifies serfdom.

statements.text: No knowledge is neutral: what a society counts as true reflects who holds power in it.
statements.agree: What gets treated as fact or expert knowledge reflects the interests of whoever has power, not a neutral search for truth.
statements.disagree: Some knowledge is neutral.
statements.note: About knowledge and power.

statements.text: There are universal moral truths, knowable by reason, that hold across all cultures.
statements.agree: Some things are right or wrong for everyone, in every culture and era, and we can work out which by reasoning.
statements.disagree: There are no universal moral truths, knowable by reason, that hold across all cultures.
statements.note: About moral universalism.

statements.text: Politics should aim at one common good worked out by reason, rather than balancing the competing interests of different groups.
statements.agree: There is one right answer for society that reason can find.
statements.disagree: Politics should not put one common good worked out by reason ahead of balancing the competing interests of different groups.
statements.note: About pluralism.

statements.text: The Jewish people have a right to a state of their own in the Land of Israel.
statements.agree: Jews are a people with a right to self-determination in Israel.
statements.disagree: The Jewish people do not have a right to a state of their own in the Land of Israel.
statements.note: Identifies Zionism and its opponents.

statements.text: Members of a nation's diaspora should have the right to return to its homeland and become citizens.
statements.agree: A nation's people abroad should always be able to come home as citizens.
statements.disagree: Members of a nation's diaspora should not have the right to return to its homeland and become citizens.
statements.note: About diaspora return laws.

statements.text: A national language that has fallen out of everyday use should be revived as the language of the state.
statements.agree: Reviving a nation's own language is worth the effort.
statements.disagree: A national language that has fallen out of everyday use should not be revived as the language of the state.
statements.note: About language revival.

statements.text: Workers and the public should have a democratic vote in how large companies are run.
statements.agree: Employees and the public get a real say, for example seats on company boards.
statements.disagree: Workers and the public should not have a democratic vote in how large companies are run.
statements.note: About economic democracy and codetermination, separate from who owns the firm.

statements.text: Parents should receive public vouchers to spend on any school they choose.
statements.agree: Public education money follows the child to whichever school the family picks.
statements.disagree: Parents should not receive public vouchers to spend on any school they choose.
statements.note: About school choice and who provides education.

statements.text: Governments should avoid running large budget deficits to stimulate the economy.
statements.agree: Governments should not run large budget deficits to stimulate the economy.
statements.disagree: Governments should not avoid running large budget deficits to stimulate the economy.
statements.note: About fiscal stimulus and public debt.

statements.text: Political freedom cannot last without economic freedom.
statements.agree: Free citizens need the freedom to own property, trade and choose work; state control of the economy ends in state control of everything.
statements.disagree: Political freedom can last without economic freedom.
statements.note: About whether free markets and free politics depend on each other.

statements.text: Government should rely on the moral example of its rulers more than on laws and punishments.
statements.agree: Leaders who live virtuously and set an example do more to order society than penalties do.
statements.disagree: Government should not rely on the moral example of its rulers more than on laws and punishments.
statements.note: About whether order comes from character or from law.

statements.text: Every nation has the right to govern itself in its own state.
statements.agree: A people with a shared identity is entitled to its own self-governing state.
statements.disagree: Not every nation has the right to govern itself in its own state.
statements.note: About national self-determination.

statements.text: My country should be willing to use force abroad without approval from the UN Security Council.
statements.agree: A country can act militarily on its own judgment even if the UN does not authorize it.
statements.disagree: My country should not be willing to use force abroad without approval from the UN Security Council.
statements.note: About acting without international approval.

statements.text: Reason, not faith or emotion, should be the only guide to knowledge and action.
statements.agree: Beliefs and choices should rest on evidence and logic, not on revelation, tradition or feeling.
statements.disagree: Reason should not take the place of faith and emotion as the only guide to knowledge and action.
statements.note: About what should ground our beliefs and choices.

statements.text: Welfare benefits should be reserved for citizens rather than extended to immigrants.
statements.agree: Welfare benefits should go to citizens, not to immigrants.
statements.disagree: Reserving welfare benefits for citizens should not take priority over extending them to immigrants.
statements.note: About who the welfare state is for.

statements.text: People who are able to work should be required to do so in order to receive welfare benefits.
statements.agree: Benefits for those who can work come with a job, training or job-search requirement.
statements.disagree: People who are able to work should not be required to do so in order to receive welfare benefits.
statements.note: About whether welfare should come with conditions.

statements.text: Employers and workers should cooperate as partners rather than struggle as opposed classes.
statements.agree: Business owners and employees share an interest and should settle differences through cooperation.
statements.disagree: Cooperation between employers and workers as partners should not take priority over class struggle.
statements.note: About whether labor and capital are partners or opponents.

statements.text: Museums, libraries and other inherited cultural institutions should be sacrificed if they hold back new creation.
statements.agree: Old institutions matter less than room for the new, and may be swept away.
statements.disagree: Museums, libraries and other inherited cultural institutions should not be sacrificed if they hold back new creation.
statements.note: About whether cultural heritage should yield to novelty.

statements.text: Countries that see themselves as dominated by the leading Western powers should form a common front against them.
statements.agree: Countries that feel dominated by Western powers should band together to resist them.
statements.disagree: Countries that see themselves as dominated by the leading Western powers should not form a common front against them.
statements.note: About whether non-Western or resisting countries should act as a bloc.

statements.text: The working class should organize along national lines rather than as an international class.
statements.agree: Workers of each country should organize within their own nation, not across borders.
statements.disagree: National organization of the working class should not take priority over its organization as an international class.
statements.note: About whether class or nation is the main unit of solidarity.

statements.text: Law should reflect distinct roles for men and women in public life.
statements.agree: Laws and customs treat men and women differently in public roles.
statements.disagree: Law should not reflect distinct roles for men and women in public life.
statements.note: About whether the law should assign different public roles by sex.

statements.text: Lending money at interest should be prohibited by law.
statements.agree: Charging interest on loans is banned by law.
statements.disagree: Lending money at interest should be legal.
statements.note: About whether lending at interest should be allowed.

statements.text: The law should classify people by race and keep the races separate in where they live, study and use public facilities.
statements.agree: The state sorts people into racial groups and enforces separate neighbourhoods, schools and public spaces.
statements.disagree: The law should not classify people by race and keep the races separate in where they live, study and use public facilities.
statements.note: About legally enforced racial classification and separation.

statements.text: The state is essentially a tool by which the ruling class dominates the others.
statements.agree: Laws, police and government mainly serve the interests of whoever owns the economy and holds power.
statements.disagree: The state is not essentially a tool by which the ruling class dominates the others.
statements.note: About whose interests the state really serves.

statements.text: Domestic oil, gas and coal production should be expanded.
statements.agree: Drill and mine more oil, gas and coal at home.
statements.disagree: Domestic oil, gas and coal production should not be expanded.
statements.note: About energy supply versus climate.

statements.text: Immigrants should be expected to give up their original culture and assimilate into the national culture.
statements.agree: Newcomers should adopt the host nation's culture and leave their own behind.
statements.disagree: Immigrants should not be expected to give up their original culture and assimilate into the national culture.
statements.note: About assimilation versus keeping other cultures.

statements.text: Elites are deliberately promoting mass immigration to replace or weaken the native population.
statements.agree: Powerful elites are steering immigration to undermine the native population.
statements.disagree: Elites are not deliberately promoting mass immigration to replace or weaken the native population.
statements.note: About whether immigration is a deliberate elite plan.

statements.text: Legislative seats should be allocated to parties in proportion to the votes they receive.
statements.agree: A party with a fifth of the votes gets about a fifth of the seats.
statements.disagree: Legislative seats should not be allocated to parties in proportion to the votes they receive.
statements.note: About how votes should turn into seats.

statements.text: My country has a special mission to spread its form of government to other peoples.
statements.agree: Our nation has a calling to bring its political system and values to others.
statements.disagree: My country does not have a special mission to spread its form of government to other peoples.
statements.note: About national mission and exceptionalism.

statements.text: Society is organized so as to systematically advantage men over women.
statements.agree: Laws, institutions and customs still favor men over women.
statements.disagree: Society is not organised so as to systematically advantage men over women.
statements.note: About whether sex-based hierarchy is built into society.

statements.text: Political elites are corrupt and out of touch with ordinary people.
statements.agree: Those in power mostly serve themselves and no longer understand or represent ordinary citizens.
statements.disagree: Political elites are not corrupt and out of touch with ordinary people.
statements.note: About whether the political class is corrupt and detached from voters.

statements.text: The state should discourage or prevent people with heritable defects from having children.
statements.agree: Public policy, such as sterilization or incentives, should reduce the passing on of inherited disabilities.
statements.disagree: The state should not discourage or prevent people with heritable defects from having children.
statements.note: About whether the state should steer who has children.

statements.text: Governments should be held legally accountable for past killings and abuses committed by their security forces.
statements.agree: Officials and officers responsible for past abuses should face courts, including international ones, however long ago.
statements.disagree: Governments should not be held legally accountable for past killings and abuses committed by their security forces.
statements.note: About whether states answer for past violence.

statements.text: Government should be limited to defending the country, enforcing justice and protecting property.
statements.agree: The state keeps to the army, courts and police, and leaves the rest to individuals and markets.
statements.disagree: Government should not be limited to defending the country, enforcing justice and protecting property.
statements.note: About how narrow the proper functions of the state are.

statements.text: Marriage and having children across racial lines should be discouraged.
statements.agree: Racial groups should mostly marry and have children within their own group.
statements.disagree: Marriage and having children across racial lines should not be discouraged.
statements.note: About whether race should shape family life.

statements.text: All people are of equal moral worth and should have equal rights before the law.
statements.agree: Everyone counts the same, and the law should treat every person as an equal whatever their birth or status.
statements.disagree: Not all people are of equal moral worth with equal rights before the law.
statements.note: About whether people are equals in worth and before the law.

statements.text: Socialism cannot be lasting in one country alone; it requires revolution in other countries too.
statements.agree: A socialist country stays vulnerable and tends to degenerate unless revolution spreads abroad.
statements.disagree: Socialism can be lasting in one country alone; it does not require revolution in other countries too.
statements.note: About whether socialism can survive in isolation.

statements.text: A state created by settlement from abroad that displaced the existing population is a colonial project.
statements.agree: Settling a land and displacing its people is colonialism, whatever the settlers' motives.
statements.disagree: A state created by settlement from abroad that displaced the existing population is not a colonial project.
statements.note: About how to classify states founded by settlement.

statements.text: All citizens should be governed by the same civil laws regardless of their religion.
statements.agree: Marriage, inheritance and family law are the same for everyone, not set by each religious community.
statements.disagree: All citizens should not be governed by the same civil laws regardless of their religion.
statements.note: About one common law versus religious personal law.

statements.text: Religious conversion should be restricted by law.
statements.agree: The law limits or polices changing religion, for example to prevent pressure or inducement.
statements.disagree: Religious conversion should be free of legal restriction.
statements.note: About limits on religious conversion.

statements.text: The slaughter of cattle should be banned by law.
statements.agree: Killing cows and similar cattle is outlawed.
statements.disagree: The slaughter of cattle should be legal.
statements.note: About legal protection of animals held sacred.

statements.text: State schools should not provide religious instruction.
statements.agree: Publicly run schools teach no religion as doctrine; faith teaching is left to families and churches.
statements.disagree: State schools may provide religious instruction.
statements.note: About religion in public education.

statements.text: A socialist state should grow stronger, not wither away, for as long as it is surrounded by hostile states.
statements.agree: While rival powers threaten it, the state keeps and strengthens its army, police and intelligence services.
statements.disagree: A socialist state should not put growing stronger ahead of withering away, even while it is surrounded by hostile states.
statements.note: About whether the state shrinks or grows on the road to communism.

statements.text: Political authority is legitimate only if it rests on the consent of the governed.
statements.agree: Rulers have a right to rule only because the people they rule have agreed to it.
statements.disagree: Consent of the governed is not the only basis of legitimate political authority.
statements.note: About where a government gets its right to rule.

statements.text: A country should aim to export more than it imports.
statements.agree: A trade surplus is a sign of national strength and something policy should pursue.
statements.disagree: A country should not aim to export more than it imports.
statements.note: About whether trade surpluses are a national goal.

statements.text: A government may require or pressure members of a minority seen as hostile to leave the country.
statements.agree: A state can move or push out a hostile minority, with or without compensation, to protect itself.
statements.disagree: A government may not require or pressure members of a minority seen as hostile to leave the country.
statements.note: About whether states may remove populations.

statements.text: It is always wrong to initiate force against another person or their property, whatever the goal.
statements.agree: Starting force against another person or their property is always wrong, whatever the goal.
statements.disagree: It is not always wrong to initiate force against another person or their property, whatever the goal.
statements.note: About whether good ends can justify starting force.

statements.text: Competition and struggle, between individuals and between peoples, are the main engine of human progress.
statements.agree: Competition and struggle, between individuals and between peoples, drive human progress more than anything else.
statements.disagree: Competition and struggle, between individuals and between peoples, are not the main engine of human progress.
statements.note: About whether competition or cooperation drives progress.

statements.text: A government may outlaw political parties that seek to abolish its constitutional order.
statements.agree: A state can ban parties whose aim is to overthrow the system, to protect it.
statements.disagree: Parties that seek to abolish a country's constitutional order should be free to organize.
statements.note: About whether free politics can restrict its enemies.

statements.text: A person is not free if someone else has the power to interfere in their life arbitrarily, even if that power is never used.
statements.agree: Freedom means not living at anyone's mercy, even a kind master.
statements.disagree: A person is not unfree merely because someone else has the power to interfere in their life arbitrarily, if that power is never used.
statements.note: About whether unused power over you limits your freedom.

statements.text: Political power should be divided among separate bodies that check one another.
statements.agree: Splitting power between branches and levels protects people from abuse.
statements.disagree: Political power should not be divided among separate bodies that check one another.
statements.note: About whether power should be divided or concentrated.

statements.text: The working class will not reach revolutionary politics on its own; it needs a disciplined party of committed revolutionaries to lead it.
statements.agree: A tightly organized party of dedicated activists must bring political direction to workers.
statements.disagree: The working class may reach revolutionary politics on its own, without a disciplined party of committed revolutionaries to lead it.
statements.note: About whether a movement needs a vanguard to lead it.

statements.text: Laws and institutions should give first priority to the needs of the poor.
statements.agree: Policy should be judged first by how it serves the poorest, even at some cost to others.
statements.disagree: Laws and institutions should not give first priority to the needs of the poor.
statements.note: About whether the poor deserve first call on society's attention.

statements.text: Council tenants should have a legal right to buy their homes.
statements.agree: Tenants of publicly owned housing can buy it, usually at a discount.
statements.disagree: Council tenants should not have a legal right to buy their homes.
statements.note: About ownership of public housing.

statements.text: The law should restrict strikes and picketing, for example by requiring secret ballots.
statements.agree: Strike action should be limited by law, such as ballots before a strike and limits on picketing.
statements.disagree: The law should not restrict strikes and picketing, for example by requiring secret ballots.
statements.note: About how far the law should limit industrial action.

statements.text: Population growth, not social institutions, is the main cause of lasting poverty.
statements.agree: Too many people for the available resources is what keeps poverty in place.
statements.disagree: Population growth is not the main cause of lasting poverty.
statements.note: About what causes poverty.

statements.text: Ethnic and racial diversity makes a society less cohesive and more prone to conflict.
statements.agree: Societies with more ethnic and racial diversity hold together less well and have more conflict.
statements.disagree: Ethnic and racial diversity does not make a society less cohesive or more prone to conflict.
statements.note: About whether diversity helps or harms social cohesion.

statements.text: Public offices should be filled by lottery among citizens rather than by election.
statements.agree: Public offices should be filled by lottery among citizens.
statements.disagree: Lottery among citizens should not replace election as the way to fill public offices.
statements.note: About how rulers should be chosen.

statements.text: In a national emergency, a government may suspend ordinary legal protections to defeat its internal enemies.
statements.agree: Courts and rights can be set aside or sped up when the state faces a mortal threat from within.
statements.disagree: Ordinary legal protections should hold even in a national emergency.
statements.note: About whether emergencies justify setting aside the rule of law.

statements.text: Governments should fix maximum prices for essential foods in times of scarcity.
statements.agree: Legal price ceilings keep basic food affordable when supplies are short, even if sellers object.
statements.disagree: Governments should not fix maximum prices for essential foods, even in times of scarcity.
statements.note: About whether the state should cap prices of necessities.

statements.text: News media and online information should be controlled by the government or ruling party.
statements.agree: Authorities decide what the press and the internet may publish.
statements.disagree: News media and online information should not be controlled by the government or ruling party.
statements.note: About state control of information.

statements.text: The armed forces should be commanded by the ruling party rather than by the state.
statements.agree: The army answers to the governing party first, not to a neutral state or parliament.
statements.disagree: Command of the armed forces by the ruling party should not replace command by the state.
statements.note: About party versus state control of the military.

statements.text: Immigrants should have to live in a country for many years before they can become citizens.
statements.agree: Immigrants should have to live in a country for many years before becoming citizens.
statements.disagree: Immigrants should not have to live in a country for many years before they can become citizens.
statements.note: About how long newcomers wait for full membership.

statements.text: Elected representatives should be paid no more than an average worker.
statements.agree: Those who hold public office are paid no more than an average worker.
statements.disagree: Elected representatives should not be paid no more than an average worker.
statements.note: About how much pay public office should carry.

statements.text: Members of a political party should be bound to carry out its decisions once they have been debated and adopted.
statements.agree: Members argue freely first, then all act together on the decision, even those who opposed it.
statements.disagree: Members of a political party should not be bound to carry out its decisions once they have been debated and adopted.
statements.note: About how much a party can demand of its members.

statements.text: Nations should pool part of their sovereignty in a supranational union such as the European Union.
statements.agree: Countries share some decisions in common institutions that can bind them, to act together on big problems.
statements.disagree: Nations should not pool part of their sovereignty in a supranational union.
statements.note: About how far nations should hand power to a shared body.

statements.text: The head of state, not the legislature, should command the armed forces and choose the government's ministers.
statements.agree: The ruler or president controls the military and picks ministers without needing the legislature's approval.
statements.disagree: The head of state should not take the place of the legislature in commanding the armed forces and choosing the government's ministers.
statements.note: About who holds executive power.

statements.text: The national church should be governed by bishops rather than by congregations or elected assemblies.
statements.agree: Senior clergy appointed from above set the church's rules and teaching.
statements.disagree: Governance of the national church by bishops should not replace governance by congregations or elected assemblies.
statements.note: About how a church should be run.

statements.text: Senior religious scholars should hold the highest political authority.
statements.agree: The most learned religious jurists have the final say over the state and its laws.
statements.disagree: Senior religious scholars should not hold the highest political authority.
statements.note: About who should hold final power in the state.

statements.text: In a war between rival great powers, working people should work for their own government's defeat rather than support it.
statements.agree: Ordinary people owe their own rulers no loyalty in a war between empires and should use it to weaken them.
statements.disagree: In a war between rival great powers, working people should not work for their own government's defeat.
statements.note: About loyalty to country versus class in wartime.

statements.text: Art, poetry and stories should be censored if they harm citizens' moral character.
statements.agree: Public authorities may restrict art and stories that shape people toward vice.
statements.disagree: Art, poetry and stories should not be censored if they harm citizens' moral character.
statements.note: About whether the state should police culture for moral effect.

statements.text: A president should be allowed to stand for re-election without limit.
statements.agree: Voters, not term limits, should decide how long a leader serves.
statements.disagree: A president should be limited in how many times he or she may stand for re-election.
statements.note: About whether leaders should face limits on how long they can serve.

statements.text: Voters should be able to remove elected officials from office before their term ends.
statements.agree: Voters can recall officials mid-term if they lose confidence in them.
statements.disagree: Elected officials should serve out their full terms.
statements.note: About how much control voters keep between elections.

statements.text: My country should end its permanent military alliances and bring its troops home from abroad.
statements.agree: Allies should defend themselves and troops should come home.
statements.disagree: My country should not end its permanent military alliances and bring its troops home from abroad.
statements.note: About whether to keep permanent military commitments overseas.

statements.text: No one should be allowed to rent out housing; every family should own the home it lives in.
statements.agree: Housing should be owned by those who live in it, not rented for profit.
statements.disagree: It should be permitted to rent out housing.
statements.note: About whether housing should be rented at all.

statements.text: A professional army should be replaced by an armed citizenry.
statements.agree: Defense should rest with armed ordinary citizens, not a standing force.
statements.disagree: A professional army should not be replaced by an armed citizenry.
statements.note: About who should hold the means of force.

statements.text: Rural life is morally healthier than life in cities.
statements.agree: Living close to the land builds character and community that city life tends to wear down.
statements.disagree: Rural life is not morally healthier than life in cities.
statements.note: About whether where people live shapes their virtue.

statements.text: A nation divided between states by a border drawn by an outside power should be reunified as one state.
statements.agree: A people split by an imposed border should be brought together in a single state.
statements.disagree: A nation divided between states by a border drawn by an outside power should not be reunified as one state.
statements.note: About partition and reunification.

statements.text: University-educated people tend to be out of touch with the realities of ordinary life.
statements.agree: People with advanced schooling are cut off from how ordinary people live and work.
statements.disagree: University-educated people are not especially out of touch with the realities of ordinary life.
statements.note: About whether education separates people from the public.

statements.text: No culture or civilization is higher or lower than another; they are only different.
statements.agree: Cultures can be different but none is more advanced or better than the others.
statements.disagree: Some cultures or civilizations are higher or lower than others.
statements.note: About ranking cultures against each other.

statements.text: The state should be able to execute people convicted of the gravest crimes, such as terrorism.
statements.agree: The worst crimes can be punished by death.
statements.disagree: The state should be barred from executing people convicted of the gravest crimes, such as terrorism.
statements.note: About capital punishment.

statements.text: School curricula should include sex education and gender equality.
statements.agree: Schools should teach pupils about sex and about equality between the sexes.
statements.disagree: School curricula should not include sex education and gender equality.
statements.note: About what schools should teach on sex and gender.

statements.text: Public schools should teach creationism or intelligent design alongside evolution.
statements.agree: Schools present creation or design accounts of origins next to evolutionary science.
statements.disagree: Public schools should not teach creationism or intelligent design alongside evolution.
statements.note: About how schools should teach the origin of life.

statements.text: Pornography should be restricted by law.
statements.agree: The law limits the making or sale of pornography, as obscenity or harm to society.
statements.disagree: Pornography should be free of legal restriction.
statements.note: About whether the state should restrict pornography.

statements.text: Citizenship should pass by descent from citizen parents rather than by birth on the territory.
statements.agree: Children of citizens are citizens wherever they are born; birth on the soil alone does not confer it.
statements.disagree: Citizenship by descent from citizen parents should not replace citizenship by birth on the territory.
statements.note: About who counts as a citizen by birth.

statements.text: Governments should support minority languages in schools, public services and elections.
statements.agree: The state provides teaching, services and ballots in minority languages.
statements.disagree: Governments should not support minority languages in schools, public services and elections.
statements.note: About state support for minority languages.

statements.text: Members of religious minorities should be exempt from general laws that burden their religious practice.
statements.agree: Believers can be excused from rules, such as dress or work-day rules, that conflict with their faith.
statements.disagree: Religious minorities should not be exempt from general laws that burden their practice.
statements.note: About exemptions from general law for religious practice.

statements.text: Social pressure to conform to custom harms human development as much as the law does, and eccentric ways of living should be encouraged.
statements.agree: Pressure to follow custom stunts individuality, so unusual ways of living deserve encouragement.
statements.disagree: Eccentric ways of living should not be encouraged on the grounds that social pressure to conform harms human development as much as the law does.
statements.note: About conformity versus individuality.

statements.text: The foreign debts of poor countries should be cancelled rather than repaid.
statements.agree: Debts owed by poor countries to rich states and lenders are written off.
statements.disagree: The foreign debts of poor countries should not be cancelled.
statements.note: About whether poor countries' external debt should be forgiven.

statements.text: Political independence means little unless the economic and property system is also transformed.
statements.agree: Without changing who owns and controls the economy, a flag and a seat in the UN change little.
statements.disagree: Political independence means something even if the economic and property system is not also transformed.
statements.note: About national freedom versus economic transformation.

statements.text: The constitution should be rewritten by a democratically elected constituent assembly.
statements.agree: A new constitution should be drafted by an assembly the people elect for that purpose.
statements.disagree: The constitution should not be rewritten by a democratically elected constituent assembly.
statements.note: About how a country should remake its constitution.

statements.text: A country may restrict political freedoms for a time to secure rapid economic development.
statements.agree: Limiting political freedoms for a period is a fair price for fast growth.
statements.disagree: A country may not restrict political freedoms for a time to secure rapid economic development.
statements.note: About trading political freedom for development.

statements.text: Wealthy countries have a duty to give substantial aid to the world's poor, wherever those people live.
statements.agree: Distance and nationality do not weaken the duty of the rich to help the poor abroad.
statements.disagree: Wealthy countries have no duty to give substantial aid to the world's poor abroad.
statements.note: About obligations to people in other countries.

statements.text: My country should maintain its own independent nuclear weapons rather than rely on an ally's protection.
statements.agree: Our country keeps its own nuclear deterrent so its defence does not depend on another state.
statements.disagree: My country should not keep its own nuclear weapons instead of relying on an ally's protection.
statements.note: About national nuclear independence.

statements.text: The head of state should be elected directly by the people rather than by parliament or an electoral college.
statements.agree: The president or equivalent is chosen in a vote of all citizens.
statements.disagree: Direct election of the head of state should not replace choice by parliament or an electoral college.
statements.note: About how the head of state is chosen.

statements.text: Central banks should be independent of elected governments and aim mainly at stable prices.
statements.agree: Monetary policy is set by an independent bank whose main goal is stable prices.
statements.disagree: Central banks should not be independent of elected governments and aim mainly at stable prices.
statements.note: About who controls money and what it is for.

statements.text: A country should not give up land it claims as its historic homeland in exchange for peace agreements.
statements.agree: Land claimed as the historic homeland is not traded away, even for peace.
statements.disagree: A country may give up land it claims as its historic homeland in exchange for peace agreements.
statements.note: About trading territory for peace.

statements.text: Private property is justified only so far as it serves the common good.
statements.agree: Owners hold property as a trust for the community, and the community may limit its use.
statements.disagree: Private property is not justified only so far as it serves the common good.
statements.note: About the social duties attached to ownership.

statements.text: The Soviet Union was a state-capitalist society, not a socialist one.
statements.agree: Soviet state ownership kept wage labor and exploitation under a bureaucratic ruling class.
statements.disagree: The Soviet Union was not a state-capitalist society.
statements.note: About what kind of society the USSR was.

statements.text: Governments should act on environmental risks even before there is scientific certainty that harm will occur.
statements.agree: Lack of full certainty is no reason to delay protective action.
statements.disagree: Governments should not act on environmental risks before there is scientific certainty that harm will occur.
statements.note: About acting on uncertain environmental risks.

statements.text: An armed attack on one allied country should be treated as an attack on all of them.
statements.agree: Allies are bound to defend one another against armed attack.
statements.disagree: An armed attack on one allied country should not be treated as an attack on all of them.
statements.note: About mutual-defense commitments between allies.

statements.text: A territory annexed without the consent of its people remains under unlawful occupation.
statements.agree: Annexation without consent never becomes legitimate, however long it lasts.
statements.disagree: A territory annexed without the consent of its people does not remain under unlawful occupation.
statements.note: About the status of territory taken without its people's consent.

statements.text: The state should curb the power and property of religious institutions and place the clergy under civil authority.
statements.agree: Religious bodies answer to the civil state, which may limit their wealth and independence.
statements.disagree: The state should not curb the power and property of religious institutions or place the clergy under civil authority.
statements.note: About how far the state may control churches.

statements.text: A head of state should stand above party politics as a symbol of national unity.
statements.agree: The nation's figurehead is non-partisan and belongs to everyone.
statements.disagree: A head of state should not stand above party politics as a symbol of national unity.
statements.note: About whether the head of state is a unifying symbol or a political actor.

statements.text: A country may use military force to prevent a region from separating from it.
statements.agree: A state may defend its territorial integrity by force if a region tries to leave.
statements.disagree: A country may not use military force to prevent a region from separating from it.
statements.note: About force and territorial integrity.

statements.text: A region could join a larger state while keeping its own economic and legal system and a high degree of autonomy.
statements.agree: A region can be part of a country yet keep its own laws, economy and self-government.
statements.disagree: A region could not join a larger state while keeping its own economic and legal system and a high degree of autonomy.
statements.note: About autonomy arrangements inside a state.

statements.text: The head of state should be regarded as sacred and of divine descent.
statements.agree: The ruler is holy, of divine origin, and that is where their authority comes from.
statements.disagree: The head of state should not be regarded as sacred and of divine descent.
statements.note: About divine status for rulers.

statements.text: Income tax rates should be flat, charging everyone the same percentage rather than rising with income.
statements.agree: Everyone pays the same percentage of their income in tax.
statements.disagree: Income tax should not charge everyone the same percentage regardless of income.
statements.note: About flat versus progressive income taxes.

statements.text: A person's character is formed mainly by upbringing and circumstances rather than by innate nature.
statements.agree: People become who they are through education and surroundings, so changing those changes people.
statements.disagree: A person's character is not formed mainly by upbringing and circumstances; innate nature matters at least as much.
statements.note: About nature versus nurture in human character.

statements.text: The ruler should not be bound by the laws that he or his predecessors made.
statements.agree: The sovereign makes the law and stands above it.
statements.disagree: The ruler should be bound by the laws that he or his predecessors made.
statements.note: About whether rulers are subject to positive law.

statements.text: Expanding humanity into space should be a central goal of civilization.
statements.agree: Civilization should aim to spread into space.
statements.disagree: Expanding humanity into space should not be a central goal of civilization.
statements.note: About space expansion as a civilizational goal.

statements.text: The best constitution mixes rule by the few and rule by the many rather than giving power to either alone.
statements.agree: A blend of aristocratic and popular elements gives the most stable government.
statements.disagree: The best constitution is not a mix of rule by the few and rule by the many.
statements.note: About mixed government.

statements.text: A national leader may be honoured in public life through portraits, statues and mass praise as the embodiment of the nation.
statements.agree: Public honours and displays of devotion to the leader are a fitting expression of national unity.
statements.disagree: A national leader may not be honoured in public life through portraits, statues and mass praise as the embodiment of the nation.
statements.note: About leader worship in public life.

statements.text: Courts should presume that children of separated parents spend equal time with each parent.
statements.agree: Equal shared parenting is the starting point unless there is a reason against it.
statements.disagree: Courts should not presume that children of separated parents spend equal time with each parent.
statements.note: About custody after separation.

statements.text: Class struggle continues under socialism, and party leaders may themselves restore capitalism.
statements.agree: Even after a socialist revolution, class conflict persists and officials can become a new privileged class.
statements.disagree: It is not true that class struggle continues under socialism and that party leaders may themselves restore capitalism.
statements.note: About class conflict after a revolution.

statements.text: Large landed estates should be taken from their owners and given to the people who farm the land.
statements.agree: Land belongs to those who work it, so big estates should be broken up and redistributed.
statements.disagree: Large landed estates should not be taken from their owners and given to the people who farm the land.
statements.note: About land reform.

statements.text: Refugees who fled or were expelled from a conflict should be allowed to return to the homes they left, and their descendants too.
statements.agree: Displaced people and their descendants have a right to return to their homes.
statements.disagree: Refugees who fled or were expelled from a conflict, and their descendants, should not be allowed to return to the homes they left.
statements.note: About a right of return for refugees.

statements.text: A state may claim territory outside its borders because people of its nationality live there.
statements.agree: Land inhabited by a state's own nationality can rightfully be claimed by that state.
statements.disagree: A state may not claim territory outside its borders because people of its nationality live there.
statements.note: About irredentist claims.

statements.text: Leaving one's religion should be punishable by law.
statements.agree: Abandoning the faith is a crime that the state may punish.
statements.disagree: People must be free to leave their religion without legal penalty.
statements.note: About apostasy.

statements.text: The law should require women to cover themselves fully in public.
statements.agree: The law requires women to cover themselves fully in public.
statements.disagree: The law should not require women to cover themselves fully in public.
statements.note: About compulsory covering of women.

statements.text: A single currency shared by several countries is better than separate national currencies.
statements.agree: A shared currency makes trade easier and binds countries together.
statements.disagree: A single currency shared by several countries is not better than separate national currencies.
statements.note: About monetary union.

statements.text: Peoples who share a language family and ancestry should work toward political unity across existing borders.
statements.agree: Kindred peoples should unite politically despite current borders.
